Staffing for care providers

Most people come to us with one of four problems. Find yours below, or ring us and we'll work it out together.

Need someone today?
020 3488 8172

  • "Someone's called in sick for tonight"

    Urgent and same-day cover. Phone is quickest, because we can start calling workers while we talk.

    Urgent cover

  • "We're short every weekend in December"

    Temporary staffing booked ahead: single shifts, block bookings with the same workers, or a long line while you recruit.

    Temporary staffing

  • "We can't open the night shift without a nurse"

    Agency RGN, RMN and RNLD nurses, matched to the kind of service you run.

    Agency nurses

  • "We need to stop relying on agency"

    Permanent recruitment for nurses, managers and senior carers.

    Permanent recruitment

What affects the price

We don't publish a price list, because the same shift can cost quite different amounts depending on a handful of things. What we do instead is agree the rates with you in writing before anyone starts. These are the things that move the number:

  • The role. A registered nurse costs more than a healthcare assistant or support worker.
  • When the shift is. Nights, weekends and bank holidays are charged at higher rates.
  • How much notice you give. Same-day requests can cost more, and they are harder to fill.
  • How much you book. A run of shifts is easier to plan than scattered single ones.
  • Specialist skills. The more specific the requirement, the fewer people can do it.
  • How you buy. NHS buyers booking through HealthTrust Europe or NHS Wales frameworks pay framework rates.

What every client gets

  • Terms and rates agreed in writing before the first shift
  • People matched to your setting, not just the job title
  • The worker's name and start time in writing for each booking
  • A short profile of the worker before the shift
  • One named person at Aviteus who knows your service
  • If someone isn't right for your service, we won't send them again, and we'll look for a replacement

Before you book

Do I have to sign a contract?

Yes, a short one. The law requires an agency to agree terms with a client in writing before it supplies staff. It covers rates, how bookings and cancellations work, and any fee if you later take on one of our workers directly.

Is there a minimum booking?

No. Once the agreement is in place you can book a single shift.

Can we offer one of your workers a permanent job?

Yes. The terms are in your client agreement. Talk to us before you make the offer.

Where do you cover?

Anywhere in the UK. Send your postcode and we'll tell you honestly how much choice we have nearby.

Want to see how we check people first? Read our compliance details, or the checklist we'd use if we were booking agency staff ourselves.

Tell us what you need

A two-minute form, or a phone call if it's urgent.
